questions.q: Why is resourcedb hidden from sys.databases and read-only?
options: It holds all system objects in an isolated file so a version upgrade can replace it cleanly without touching master or user data
Because Microsoft forgot to expose it in newer versions
Because it holds no data and serves no purpose in modern SQL Server
Because it's only used by SQL Server Agent
questions.explain: Before SQL Server 2005's resourcedb design, system objects lived inside master and every service pack had to carefully script changes into it. resourcedb isolates that entirely.

questions.q: What actually happens when you run CREATE DATABASE?
options: SQL Server copies the model database to create the new one
SQL Server builds a completely empty database with no reference to any other database
SQL Server copies resourcedb to create the new one
SQL Server copies master to create the new one
questions.explain: model is the literal template — any object or setting present in model is copied into every subsequently created database.

questions.q: Where does SQL Server Agent store its job definitions, schedules, and job history?
options: msdb
tempdb
resourcedb
model
questions.explain: msdb holds Agent job definitions, schedules, history, alerts, operators, backup/restore history, and Database Mail configuration.

questions.q: What is unique about tempdb compared to the other system databases?
options: It is recreated from scratch at every instance restart and is never restored from a backup
It is the only system database that is hidden from sys.databases
It cannot hold any user-created objects
It is backed up automatically every time the instance starts
questions.explain: tempdb starts fresh at its configured initial size on every restart, holding temp objects, work tables for sorts/hashes, and the version store.

questions.q: Why does master matter even though it holds no user data?
options: It records instance-level metadata, including the list of every other database and where its files live — without it, the instance can't start
It stores every row of every user table as a hidden backup
It is only used for SQL Server Agent job history
It has no real function and can be safely deleted
questions.explain: master holds logins, linked server definitions, endpoints, and the catalog of every database on the instance — the instance needs it just to know what else exists.
